cards.text: The ark of God has arrived, and they set it inside the tent that David, king of Israel, pitched for it. Then they present burnt offerings and peace offerings before God. Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for years, so trust me: a spot set up JUST for you is a BIG deal.

cards.question: David finishes the burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then what does he do?

answers.text: He blesses the people in the name of the LORD
He reads the Law of Moses to the people
He leads the people on a march through the city

cards.text: Then David starts handing out food: a loaf of bread, a date cake and a raisin cake. Three treats and not ONE cookie, but I'm not upset, friend, I'm just saying it out loud.

cards.question: Only the men of Israel get a share of David's bread, date cake and raisin cake.

cards.text: Next, David appoints some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD. I had to appoint MYSELF to every job in my bakery, friend, so David having options? I'm a little jealous.

cards.question: What job does David give the Levites he appoints before the ark?

answers.text: To give thanks and praise the LORD
To carry the ark around the city
To repair the tent every morning

cards.text: Asaph is the chief, with a whole crew under him on harps and lyres while he sounds the cymbals. The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel blow the trumpets regularly before the ark.
On that day David first commits to Asaph and his associates a song of thanksgiving to the LORD. It opens like a to-do list: give thanks to the LORD and call on His name.

cards.question: David's song says the LORD's deeds should be made known among the nations.

cards.text: The list keeps going: sing to Him, sing praises, tell of all His wonders, glory in His holy name. I can't get FOUR things done before my oven timer goes off, and this song is just getting warmed up.

cards.question: David's song tells the people to seek the LORD's face only on feast days.

cards.text: Then the song tells the sons of Jacob, also called Israel, His chosen ones, to remember His wonders, His marvels and the judgments He has pronounced. Friend, I walk across my bakery to the oven and forget why I came, and my WHOLE planet is one bakery.

cards.question: How far does David's song say the LORD's judgments carry?

cards.text: Next the song says to remember His covenant forever, the word He ordained for a thousand generations, made with Abraham, Israel's forefather, sworn to Abraham's son Isaac and confirmed to Jacob as an everlasting covenant. A thousand generations, friend, and the warranty cards in my old junk drawer couldn't make it ONE year.

cards.question: In His covenant, God promises to give them the land of ___ as the portion of their inheritance.

cards.text: But back then they were few in number, strangers in the land, wandering from nation to nation. Few INDEED, friend, that's not a nation, that's a group chat.

cards.question: While Israel's forefathers wander from one kingdom to another, what does the LORD do?

answers.text: He lets no one oppress them
He lets them fend for themselves
He sends them into the desert

cards.question: The LORD even rebukes kings for the wanderers' sake, warning them not to touch His anointed ones.

cards.text: Now David's song turns to the whole world: sing to the LORD, all the earth, and proclaim His salvation day after day. Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among ALL peoples.

cards.question: David's song says the LORD is to be feared above all gods. What reason does it give?

answers.text: Other gods are idols but He made the heavens
Other gods are new but He was there first
Other gods are far but He is close by

cards.text: “Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and joy fill His dwelling.” My bakery has flour on the floor and a timer that beeps at me, so friend, we are NOT the same.

cards.question: David's song calls only on the people of Israel to ascribe glory and strength to the LORD.

cards.text: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name, the song goes on, and come before Him. Worship the LORD in the splendor of His holiness.

cards.question: When the families of the nations come before the LORD, what does David's song tell them to bring?

cards.text: The song says all the earth should tremble before Him, and the world is firmly established and cannot be moved. Firmly established, friend, and I can't even get my cooling rack to stop wobbling.

Then the song says: let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice, and let them say among the nations, ‘The LORD reigns!’ Let the sea resound and the fields exult too: the FIELDS, friend, and my oven timer has to beep THREE times before I even get moving.

cards.question: In David's song, the trees of the forest sing for joy before the LORD too. What reason does the song give?

answers.text: He is coming to judge the earth
The long winter is finally over
The harvest has all come in

cards.text: Then the song circles right back to where it started: give thanks to the LORD.

cards.question: Why does David's song say to give thanks to the LORD this time?

answers.text: He is good and His love lasts forever
He gave them rest from every war
He made their fields grow tall

cards.question: Near the end, David's song gives the people a cry to God to save them, gather them and deliver them. The reason it gives is so they may give thanks to His holy name.

cards.text: And the song closes: “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.” Friend, THAT is how you land a song.

cards.question: David's song of thanksgiving is done. How do all the people respond?

answers.text: They say Amen and Praise the LORD
They shout Long live King David

cards.text: So David leaves Asaph and his associates before the ark to minister there regularly, with Obed-edom and others as gatekeepers. And he leaves Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at Gibeon, presenting burnt offerings morning and evening, with Heman, Jeduthun and their musicians giving thanks to the LORD.

cards.question: Then all the people depart for their homes, and David heads home too. What does David go home to do?
